ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 makes the driver's contact obligation conjunctive: before cancelling for no-show the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message to the rider AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The trip record's own derived contact check shows call_count 2 but message_count 0, and records obligation_met as false. With the message limb missing, the fee must be voided and the rider is not charged.

The only message on the chat log before the driver cancelled is MSG-05070-001, the automated 'Your driver has arrived.' notification, whose sender field is SYSTEM and which was generated as platform telemetry. POL-NS-23 requires a message sent by the driver; a system notification is not a driver message and cannot discharge that limb.

The driver's own chat message MSG-05070-002 was sent at 16:13:55 and delivered at 16:13:58, while trip_record.cancelled_at is 16:13:40. Anything the driver sent to the rider came after the cancellation, so it cannot satisfy POL-NS-23's requirement that the message be sent before trip_record.cancelled_at.

The driver's counter-account is that he 'called 2 times and also sent message', and he adds that 'the app also sends the arrived notification automatically'. That is the driver conceding on the record that the only notification the rider received was automatic. The two in-app calls are confirmed (16:09:30 and 16:11:50, both unanswered), so the call limb is met, but the driver's own explanation leaves the message limb unmet and POL-NS-23 is not satisfied by calls alone.

Conceded for the driver: the GPS trace corroborates his arrival — the nearest fix to the pickup at 16:07:50 reports accuracy 6.0 m and a distance of 2.16 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter — and the cancellation at 16:13:40 is 375 s after arrival, past the 300 s free wait. That entitlement under POL-NS-21 lets him cancel, but it is a precondition for cancelling, not a substitute for POL-NS-23, which the record's derived check still marks as obligation_met false.

The disputed money is still with the platform and not with the rider: the payments ledger shows one cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, and the fee charged matches the policy fee of 5.00 SGD. Voiding the charge under POL-NS-23 therefore means FULL_REFUND of the whole contested 5.00 SGD to the filing rider, with no driver compensation, which is the outcome POL-NS-23 licenses.

The chat log that defeats the driver's message assertion is complete rather than fragmentary: it holds 3 entries, truncated is false, its admissibility status is COMPLETE with no issues, and its count matches trip_record.chat_message_count. There is no other artifact on this trip that carries a driver-to-rider message; the only non-platform artifact is the traffic advisory, which is MISSING with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0 and therefore carries no fact that could rehabilitate the missing message.

The POL-NS-21 precondition for a no-show cancellation was satisfied on this trip. The driver marked arrival at 16:07:25, the 300 s free wait expired at 16:12:25, and the driver did not cancel until 16:13:40 — 375 s after arrival and 75 s after the free wait ran out. The record's own free-wait computation reports cancelled_after_free_wait = true. Cancelling for no-show after the free wait is exactly what POL-NS-21 permits.

The driver actually attended the pickup, as the arrival test requires. The GPS trace (COMPLETE, weight 1.0, every fix reporting accuracy) corroborates the trip record's arrival event: the nearest fix is 2.16 m from the pickup point at 16:07:50, far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the driver's reported speed is 0 kph from 16:07:20 continuously through 16:13:20 — the vehicle was parked at the pickup for the whole wait, not passing by.

The fee charged is the fee the schedule fixes. The payments ledger shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, total_charged of 5.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, and its own derived check reports fee_matches_policy = true against the 5.00 SGD figure in POL-NS-22. Where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION with both amount fields equal to the fee charged.

The call limb of the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is squarely met. Before cancelling, the driver placed two in-app calls to the rider, at 16:09:30 (rang 25 s, unanswered) and again at 16:11:50 (rang 20 s, unanswered), both recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls and both before cancelled_at 16:13:40. The clause requires the call to have been placed, not answered, and these were placed.

On the message limb of POL-NS-23 the driver argues the clause's substance and states its difficulty plainly. The rider did receive an in-app message before cancellation: the platform delivered 'Your driver has arrived' to her in-app at 16:07:29, 25 s after the driver marked arrival, and the driver then called twice — that is the in-app warning the clause exists to give a rider before a no-show fee. The driver's own chat message ('I cancel already, you never come down') was sent at 16:13:55, 15 s after cancelled_at, so the driver does not rest on it, and to the extent POL-NS-23 is read to require a driver-authored chat message strictly before cancelled_at the record does not supply one and the driver's case must rest on the in-app arrival message standing in that place.

The no-show was genuine, not a pretext. The GPS trace carries no rider track at the pickup, and the rider's own in-app message at 16:14:30 — 'What? I was coming down now' — is an admission that she had not reached the pickup when the driver cancelled at 16:13:40. A rider still on the way after the free wait has expired is precisely the rider POL-NS-21 lets the driver cancel on, and the real-world outcome POL-NS-22 compensates is a driver who waited and was not met.

No elevated confidence applies to this file. Both profiles carry fraud_flags = 0, so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 bar is not engaged, and the contested amount of 5.00 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final. A DRIVER_COMPENSATION for the driver can therefore issue on this record rather than being held for review.

ruling.explanation:
The rider's dispute succeeds, and the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged on TRP-05070 is refunded in full.

POL-NS-23 makes the driver's contact obligation conjunctive: before cancelling for a no-show the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message to the rider AND placed at least one in-app call to her, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. The call limb is met on the record: the driver placed two in-app calls, at 16:09:30 (rang 25 s) and 16:11:50 (rang 20 s), both unanswered (EV-TRIP-05070.in_app_calls). The message limb fails. The only message before the 16:13:40 cancellation is MSG-05070-001, 'Your driver has arrived.', sent at 16:07:28 by sender SYSTEM (EV-CHAT-05070); the driver's own message, MSG-05070-002, was sent at 16:13:55, after the cancellation. The trip record's own derived contact check agrees: call_count 2, message_count 0, obligation_met false (EV-TRIP-05070). A platform arrival notification is not a message sent by the driver, so, as the rider's advocate argues, it cannot discharge a limb the clause places on the driver. With the message limb missing, POL-NS-23 voids the fee and directs a full refund of the amount charged, 5.00 SGD (EV-FARE-05070, total_charged 5.00, cancellation_fee 5.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0), with no driver compensation.

To the driver: the arguments you raised are accepted so far as they go but do not change the outcome. Your arrival at 16:07:25 is corroborated — the nearest GPS fix is 2.16 m from the pickup at 16:07:50, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius and the 25 m accuracy filter, with the vehicle at 0 kph through the wait, and the cancellation at 16:13:40 is 375 s after arrival, past the 300 s free wait; POL-NS-21 therefore entitled you to cancel, and the 5.00 SGD fee matches POL-NS-22's schedule (fee_matches_policy true). But POL-NS-21 is a precondition for cancelling, not a substitute for POL-NS-23's separate contact obligation, which the record marks unmet. Nor does the rider's 16:14:30 message ('What? I was coming down now') cure the missing driver message: whether the no-show was genuine is a different question from whether you discharged POL-NS-23, and the latter is what voids the fee.

No referral arises. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral is not triggered; you did arrive, so POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not fire; and the rider's POL-NS-25 counter (rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d) is not present on the profile, so that flag is not raised.

The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so by POL-NS-26 and POL-GEN-22 the AI ruling is final. Confidence rests on complete, weight-1.0 artifacts — the chat log (EV-CHAT-05070) and the trip record (EV-TRIP-05070), both COMPLETE with no issue codes. The one missing artifact, the traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05070-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no fact and is not relied on.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
